en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 18.25.
Saraṇaduka, Hetudukādi.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and a root-cause (*hetu*), there arises a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not a root-cause (*na-hetu*) by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … three.

Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and a root-cause, there arises a state that is without-conflict and not a root-cause by way of root-condition … one. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are four; under object-condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two … pe … under result-condition (*vipāka*) there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are four.
Dependent on a state that is with-conflict and not a root-cause, there arises a state that is without-conflict and not a root-cause by way of root-condition … one.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and not-rooted (*na-hetu*), a state that is non-refuge (*na-saraṇa*) and not-rooted arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … one. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are two … pe … under resultant [condition] there is one … pe … under non-disappearance [condition] there are two.
Dependent on a state that is with-refuge (*sa-saraṇa*) and with-root (*sa-hetu*), a state that is non-refuge and not-rooted arises by way of root-condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and with-root, a state that is non-refuge and not-rooted arises by way of root-condition.
… one. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are two; under object condition, one; under predominance condition, two … pe … under conascence condition, four;
under mutuality condition, two … pe … under result condition, one … pe … under non-disappearance condition, four.
Dependent on a state with conflict that is rootless, a state without conflict that is not rootless arises by way of root condition … one.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and rootless (*ahetuka*), there arises a state that is not without conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not rootless (*na-ahetuka*) by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). ... One. (Abbreviated. Two under the root [condition] ... pe ... one under the prenascence (*purejāta*) and repetition (*āsevana*) conditions ... pe ... one under the resultant (*vipāka*) condition ... pe ... two under the non-disappearance (*avigata*) condition.

Dependent on a state that is with conflict (*saraṇa*) and associated with a root (*hetu-sampayutta*), there arises a state that is not without conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not associated with a root (*na-hetu-sampayutta*) by way of the root condition.

... One. Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and associated with a root (*hetu-sampayutta*), there arises a state that is not without conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not associated with a root (*na-hetu-sampayutta*) ... [by way of the root condition]. ... One.
A state arises by way of root condition...

one. (Abbreviated. Under root: two; under object: one; under predominance: two... pe ... under conascence: four; under mutuality: two... pe ... under result: one... pe ... under non-disappearance: four. (Similar to the "With-root" dyad.
Dependent on a state that is with-conflict, a root, and with-root, there arises a state that is without-conflict, not a root, and not without-root, by way of root condition... one.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*), both with cause and having a cause, there arises a state that is neither-conflict nor with-cause and is neither-without-cause nor without-cause, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*) … one [formula]. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are two … pe … under resultant-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are two.

Dependent on a state that is conflict (*saraṇa*), both with cause and not itself a root, there arises a state that is neither-conflict nor without-cause and is neither-not-a-root nor without-root, by way of root-condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict, both with cause and not itself a root, there arises a state that is neither-conflict nor without-cause and is neither-not-a-root nor without-root … [one].

A cause-condition phenomenon arises by way of the root condition … one. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are two … pe … under the resultant condition there is one … pe … under the non-disappearance condition there are two.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and both a root and associated with a root, there arises a phenomenon that is without-conflict (*na-araṇa*), not a root, and dissociated from a root, by way of the root condition. (This is similar to the "Root-with-root" dyad.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*), not a root, but accompanied by a root (*sahetuka*), there arises a phenomenon that is without-conflict, not a root, and not accompanied by a root, by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict, not a root, and with root, there arises a state that is non-conflict, not a root, and without root by way of root-condition … one.
(Abbreviated. Under root there are two; under predominance there are two … pe … under mutuality there is one … pe … under resultant there is one … pe … under non-disappearance there are two.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict, non-root, and rootless, there arises a state that is non-conflict, non-root, and rootless by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there is one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there is one.
